highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Opus 5, their most capable model yet, featuring a 1M token context window and a fast mode priced at $10/$50 per million tokens. This is now the default Opus model in Claude Code, meaning your existing projects will automatically benefit from improved reasoning and longer context handling. Beginners can start using it immediately without any configuration changes.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219 Released – Opus 5 Default, Sandbox Network Allowlist
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.219 adds Claude Opus 5 as the default Opus model and introduces a new `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting that silently blocks any network host not explicitly whitelisted when running sandboxed commands. There is also a new `DirectoryAdded` hook for automating actions when directories are added to your project. Update now to get Opus 5 automatically and tighten your sandbox security with a single config line.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218 Released – /code-review Now Runs as Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The `/code-review` slash command now runs as a background subagent, so code review work no longer clutters your main conversation thread and stacked slash commands correctly target the right review scope. This is a significant workflow improvement for developers who chain multiple slash commands together. Simply type `/code-review` as usual — the change is transparent but keeps your context much cleaner.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.216 Released – Quadratic Slowdown Fix for Long Sessions
highlights.summary: This release fixes a critical performance bug where message normalization grew quadratically with conversation length, causing multi-second stalls and slow session resumes in long coding sessions. A new `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` setting also lets you skip filesystem isolation while still controlling network egress — useful when you want sandboxing without the overhead of filesystem restrictions. If you have been experiencing slowdowns in long sessions, updating to this version should resolve them immediately.

highlights.title: Show HN: A Local Merge Queue for Parallel Claude Code Agents
highlights.summary: A developer pushing up to 90 commits a day using 4-5 parallel Claude Code agents on a MacBook Air built a local merge queue to prevent agents from simultaneously running builds, tests, and dev servers and crashing the machine. The tool serializes agent output so only one agent builds or tests at a time, preventing resource exhaustion without needing paid CI minutes. If you are experimenting with parallel agents, this is a practical solution to keep your machine stable.

highlights.title: Show HN: claude-account – Switch Claude Code Accounts Without Logging In Again
highlights.summary: This small CLI tool lets you save multiple Claude Code accounts (e.g. work and personal) and switch between them instantly with a single command, bypassing the full login flow each time. Commands are intentionally simple: `claude account add myworkaccount` to save an account and a similar command to switch. A handy quality-of-life tool if you manage more than one Claude subscription.

highlights.title: Get EVERYTHING Out of Claude Code in 13 Minutes (Beginner to Pro)
highlights.summary: This YouTube video promises a fast-track walkthrough of Claude Code from absolute beginner to productive developer in just 13 minutes. It is a great starting point if you want a dense, practical overview without sitting through a multi-hour course. Watch it once to orient yourself, then revisit specific sections as you encounter new features.

highlights.title: Claude Code Creator's Greatest Tip For Using AI Agents
highlights.summary: This short YouTube video features advice directly from the creator of Claude Code on how to get the most out of AI agents, making it unusually authoritative compared to community tutorials. Even experienced users are likely to pick up a workflow insight or mental model they have not considered. Worth watching regardless of your skill level for the first-principles perspective.

tips_of_the_day: When running multiple parallel Claude Code agents, assign each agent a clearly scoped directory or module so they never edit the same files simultaneously — this alone eliminates most merge conflicts before they start.

Use `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` in your project's Claude Code config to lock down which external hosts sandboxed commands can reach, giving you a simple audit trail of any unexpected network calls your code might make.

Before starting a long coding session, run `/code-review` as a background subagent on your current branch — it will analyse your work in the background while you keep coding, so feedback is ready the moment you want it.
